reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing and replaying the record, returned to the 2026–2027 official study guide, both start rosters and the separate graduation course pages. Reconstructed the 60/75/15/30 EC structure, rechecked the progression of compulsory projects and reconsidered actual UCR course descriptions and topics for computing, applied AI and organisational systems. Checked the finished alignment and separate network and security assessments against that evidence in this separate same-AI pass.
findings: The 2026–2027 guide distinguishes the standard Computer Science BSc from the open bachelor and Information Science. It confirms 12 compulsory 5 EC foundation courses, 15 compulsory 5 EC advanced taught courses, a 15 EC graduation project and 30 EC of free electives. The curriculum totals 180 EC and is Dutch-taught, part-time and paced flexibly. The official learning lines are software technology, information systems and communication technology.

The guide provides September and February suggested part-time schedules with variable and fixed starts. Introductory programming supports advanced object-oriented work; the foundation practicum draws on programming, design and databases. Networks and algorithms prepare operating systems, and AppLab integrates upper computing work. Graduation Project Preparation (IB9902) requires the foundation plus at least twelve specified advanced courses, including the starred courses. The current project page confirms the remaining courses, including preparation and free electives, must be passed, credited or already being studied under the online study plan unless the examiner permits entry. The project involves supervised research with a thesis and presentation. The comparator comparison is organised by curriculum rather than imposing UCR semesters on OU.

The computing option combines Python and formal logic with C++ and Haskell development, databases, networks and operating systems, two successive algorithms courses, calculus, linear algebra, probability and numerical methods. Machine learning, search, decision models, reinforcement learning and imaging develop genuine applied AI breadth. The information systems option shares the necessary computing core but uses strategy, organisational behaviour, social and market research, product development, AI governance and communication to study technology adoption and effects on users. Replacing a second general statistics course with Networks & Operating Systems improves technical literacy while preserving separate quantitative and qualitative research training. The content of description-only Database Management Systems, Digital Transformation, market research and reinforcement learning supports their concrete roles. One combined networks and systems course provides genuine foundations but lacks the sequence in network engineering, infrastructure and distributed systems needed to anchor a separate communication technology direction. Cryptographic arithmetic, privacy and access-control coverage are complementary to security but do not sustain a separate cybersecurity programme. The comparison retains OU hardware, ontology, dedicated security and testing, integrated projects, and the required graduation project as visible differences. UCR offers independent research outside the planned 180 EC.
